43
I was a stranger and you did not take me in; naked and you did not clothe me; sick and in prison and you did not visit me."
ξένος xenos ἤμην ēmēn καὶ kai οὐ ou συνηγάγετέ synēgagete με, me, γυμνὸς gymnos καὶ kai οὐ ou περιεβάλετέ periebalete με, me, ἀσθενὴς asthenēs καὶ kai ἐν en φυλακῇ phylakē καὶ kai οὐκ ouk ἐπεσκέψασθέ epeskepsasthe με. me.
44
Then they also will answer, saying, "Lord, when did we see you hungry or thirsty or a stranger or naked or sick or in prison and did not serve you?"
τότε tote ἀποκριθήσονται apokrithēsontai καὶ kai αὐτοὶ autoi λέγοντες· legontes· Κύριε, Kyrie, πότε pote σε se εἴδομεν eidomen πεινῶντα peinōnta ἢ ē διψῶντα dipsōnta ἢ ē ξένον xenon ἢ ē γυμνὸν gymnon ἢ ē ἀσθενῆ asthenē ἢ ē ἐν en φυλακῇ phylakē καὶ kai οὐ ou διηκονήσαμέν diēkonēsamen σοι; soi;
45
Then he will answer them, saying, "Amen I say to you, inasmuch as you did not do it to one of the least of these, neither did you do it to me."
τότε tote ἀποκριθήσεται apokrithēsetai αὐτοῖς autois λέγων· legōn· Ἀμὴν Amēn λέγω legō ὑμῖν, hymin, ἐφ' eph' ὅσον hoson οὐκ ouk ἐποιήσατε epoiēsate ἑνὶ heni τούτων toutōn τῶν tōn ἐλαχίστων, elachistōn, οὐδὲ oude ἐμοὶ emoi ἐποιήσατε. epoiēsate.
Notes Verse 45

Textual asymmetry. eph' hoson ouk epoiēsate heni toutōn tōn elachistōn, oude emoi epoiēsate — 'inasmuch as you did it not to one of the least of these, you did it not to me'. NOTE: v.45 LACKS adelphōn mou present at v.40. The asymmetry is preserved per Gray 1989. Implications for the universalist-vs-restricted reading-debate are documented in overlay entry adelphōn-mou-presence-absence-asymmetry-mt-25-40-vs-25-45-gray.

46
And these will go away into eternal punishment, but the righteous into eternal life.
καὶ kai ἀπελεύσονται apeleusontai οὗτοι houtoi εἰς eis κόλασιν kolasin αἰώνιον, aiōnion, οἱ hoi δὲ de δίκαιοι dikaioi εἰς eis ζωὴν zōēn αἰώνιον. aiōnion.
Notes Verse 46

kai apeleusontai houtoi eis kolasin aiōnion, hoi de dikaioi eis zōēn aiōnion — 'and these will go away into eternal punishment, but the righteous into eternal life'. The Matthean parallel-structure kolasin aiōnion / zōēn aiōnion. The parallel-structure argument: if aiōnion in 'eternal life' means 'endless-eternal', then aiōnion in 'eternal punishment' must equally. The conditionalist counter-argument: parallelism does not require identical-semantic-content. The WoH-Translation preserves 'eternal' on the surface; see aiōnios-mt-25-41-46-eternal-vs-age-pertaining-cross-corpus.

Chapter 28

Matthew 28 — The Resurrection + the Great Commission

1
Now after the Sabbath, as it began to dawn toward the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary came to see the tomb.
And when he was come down from the mountain, great multitudes followed him.
Ὀψὲ Opse δὲ de σαββάτων, sabbatōn, τῇ tē ἐπιφωσκούσῃ epiphōskousē εἰς eis μίαν mian σαββάτων, sabbatōn, ἦλθεν ēlthen Μαρία Maria ἡ hē Μαγδαληνὴ Magdalēnē καὶ kai ἡ hē ἄλλη allē Μαρία Maria θεωρῆσαι theōrēsai τὸν ton τάφον. taphon.
Notes Verse 1

The Resurrection-narrative opens. Opse de sabbatōn, tē epiphōskousē eis mian sabbatōn — 'after the sabbath, as the first day of the week was dawning'. The temporal-marker establishes the early-Sunday-morning setting; the Christian first-day-of-the-week (kyriakē hēmera) tradition derives from this Synoptic dating. Mary Magdalene and 'the other Mary' (Mary mother of James + Joses per Mt 27:56) are the first-witnesses — preserved across the Synoptic-tradition (Mk 16:1; Lk 24:10; Jn 20:1).

2
And behold, there was a great earthquake; for an angel of the Lord, having come down from heaven, came and rolled away the stone, and sat upon it.
And behold, there came to him a leper and worshipped him, saying, Lord, if thou wilt, thou canst make me clean.
καὶ kai ἰδοὺ idou σεισμὸς seismos ἐγένετο egeneto μέγας· megas· ἄγγελος angelos γὰρ gar κυρίου kyriou καταβὰς katabas ἐξ ex οὐρανοῦ ouranou καὶ kai προσελθὼν proselthōn ἀπεκύλισεν apekylisen τὸν ton λίθον lithon καὶ kai ἐκάθητο ekathēto ἐπάνω epanō αὐτοῦ. autou.
Notes Verse 2

seismos egeneto megas; angelos gar kyriou katabas ex ouranou — 'a great earthquake occurred; for an angel of the Lord descending from heaven'. The Matthean-distinctive earthquake (paralleling the Mt 27:51-54 crucifixion-earthquake) is unique to Matthew. The angelos kyriou katabas ex ouranou — calques the LXX malʾakh YHWH descending; the Matthean angelophanic-pattern from Mt 1:20 + 2:13 + 2:19 + 2:22 (the four Joseph dream-revelations) continues.

3
His appearance was like lightning, and his garment white as snow.
And he stretched forth his hand, and touched him, saying, I will; be thou made clean. And straightway his leprosy was cleansed.
ἦν ēn δὲ de ἡ hē εἰδέα eidea αὐτοῦ autou ὡς hōs ἀστραπὴ astrapē καὶ kai τὸ to ἔνδυμα endyma αὐτοῦ autou λευκὸν leukon ὡς hōs χιών. chiōn.
Notes Verse 3

hē eidea autou hōs astrapē kai to endyma autou leukon hōs chiōn — 'his appearance like lightning and his clothing white as snow'. The luminous-angelic description draws on Dan 7:9 LXX (the Ancient-of-Days enthronement: clothing-white-as-snow) + Dan 10:6 LXX (the man-in-linen luminous-vision). The same vocabulary describes the Transfiguration at Mt 17:2 — Matthean intratextual-echo. See transfiguration-mt-17-1-9-elohim-manifest-in-glory-mosheh-eliyyahu-divine-presence-cross-corpus-with-disavowals.

4
And for fear of him the guards trembled and became like dead men.
And Jesus saith unto him, See thou tell no man; but go, show thyself to the priest, and offer the gift that Moses commanded, for a testimony unto them.
ἀπὸ apo δὲ de τοῦ tou φόβου phobou αὐτοῦ autou ἐσείσθησαν eseisthēsan οἱ hoi τηροῦντες tērountes καὶ kai ἐγενήθησαν egenēthēsan ὡς hōs νεκροί. nekroi.
5
But the angel answered and said to the women, "Do not be afraid, for I know that you are seeking Jesus the crucified.
And when he was entered into Capernaum, there came unto him a centurion, beseeching him,
ἀποκριθεὶς apokritheis δὲ de ὁ ho ἄγγελος angelos εἶπεν eipen ταῖς tais γυναιξίν· gynaixin· Μὴ Mē φοβεῖσθε phobeisthe ὑμεῖς, hymeis, οἶδα oida γὰρ gar ὅτι hoti Ἰησοῦν Iēsoun τὸν ton ἐσταυρωμένον estaurōmenon ζητεῖτε· zēteite·
Notes Verse 5

mē phobeisthe hymeis — 'do not be afraid'. The angelic-reassurance formula (Gen 15:1; Lk 1:13, 30; Mt 1:20). Cross-corpus to the divine-encounter-fear-formula across the Hebrew Bible.

6
He is not here, for he has been raised, just as he said. Come, see the place where he lay.
and saying, Lord, my servant lieth in the house sick of the palsy, grievously tormented.
οὐκ ouk ἔστιν estin ὧδε, hōde, ἠγέρθη ēgerthē γὰρ gar καθὼς kathōs εἶπεν· eipen· δεῦτε deute ἴδετε idete τὸν ton τόπον topon ὅπου hopou ἔκειτο. ekeito.
Notes Verse 6

ouk estin hōde, ēgerthē gar kathōs eipen — 'he is not here, for he is risen as he said'. The empty-tomb proclamation; the passive ēgerthē (he was raised) preserves the divine-passive (God raised him, not Jesus raised-himself). Cross-synoptic-parallel.

7
And go quickly and tell his disciples that he has been raised from the dead, and behold, he goes before you into Galilee; there you will see him. Behold, I have told you."
And he saith unto him, I will come and heal him.
καὶ kai ταχὺ tachy πορευθεῖσαι poreutheisai εἴπατε eipate τοῖς tois μαθηταῖς mathētais αὐτοῦ autou ὅτι hoti Ἠγέρθη Ēgerthē ἀπὸ apo τῶν tōn νεκρῶν, nekrōn, καὶ kai ἰδοὺ idou προάγει proagei ὑμᾶς hymas εἰς eis τὴν tēn Γαλιλαίαν, Galilaian, ἐκεῖ ekei αὐτὸν auton ὄψεσθε· opsesthe· ἰδοὺ idou εἶπον eipon ὑμῖν. hymin.
8
And they went away quickly from the tomb with fear and great joy, and ran to bring word to his disciples.
And the centurion answered and said, Lord, I am not worthy that thou shouldest come under my roof; but only say the word, and my servant shall be healed.
καὶ kai ἀπελθοῦσαι apelthousai ταχὺ tachy ἀπὸ apo τοῦ tou μνημείου mnēmeiou μετὰ meta φόβου phobou καὶ kai χαρᾶς charas μεγάλης megalēs ἔδραμον edramon ἀπαγγεῖλαι apangeilai τοῖς tois μαθηταῖς mathētais αὐτοῦ. autou.
9
And behold, Jesus met them, saying, "Greetings." And they came up and took hold of his feet and worshipped him.
For I also am a man under authority, having under myself soldiers: and I say to this one, Go, and he goeth; and to another, Come, and he cometh; and to my servant, Do this, and he doeth it.
καὶ kai ἰδοὺ idou Ἰησοῦς Iēsous ὑπήντησεν hypēntēsen αὐταῖς autais λέγων· legōn· Χαίρετε· Chairete· αἱ hai δὲ de προσελθοῦσαι proselthousai ἐκράτησαν ekratēsan αὐτοῦ autou τοὺς tous πόδας podas καὶ kai προσεκύνησαν prosekynēsan αὐτῷ. autō.
Notes Verse 9

kai idou Iēsous hypēntēsen autais — 'and behold, Jesus met them'. The Matthean-distinctive Jerusalem-area resurrection-appearance to the women (Mk 16:8 ends without resurrection-appearances; Lk 24 + Jn 20 have varied appearance-traditions).

10
Then Jesus said to them, "Do not be afraid. Go and tell my brothers to go into Galilee, and there they will see me."
And when Jesus heard it, he marvelled, and said to them that followed, Verily I say unto you, I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel.
τότε tote λέγει legei αὐταῖς autais ὁ ho Ἰησοῦς· Iēsous· Μὴ Mē φοβεῖσθε· phobeisthe· ὑπάγετε hypagete ἀπαγγείλατε apangeilate τοῖς tois ἀδελφοῖς adelphois μου mou ἵνα hina ἀπέλθωσιν apelthōsin εἰς eis τὴν tēn Γαλιλαίαν, Galilaian, κἀκεῖ kakei με me ὄψονται. opsontai.
Notes Verse 10

hypagete apangeilate tois adelphois mou hina apelthōsin eis tēn Galilaian, kakei me opsontai — 'go and tell my brothers to depart for Galilee, and there they will see me'. The Galilee-appearance instruction sets up the Mt 28:16-20 Great Commission scene. adelphois mou — Jesus' brothers = the disciples (paralleling Mt 12:48-50; relevant to the Mt 25:40 adelphōn mou identification-question — see sheep-and-goats-mt-25-31-46-adelphōn-mou-tōn-elachistōn-three-readings-gray-cross-corpus).

11
While they were going, behold, some of the guard came into the city and reported to the chief priests everything that had happened.
And I say unto you, that many shall come from the east and the west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven:
Πορευομένων Poreuomenōn δὲ de αὐτῶν autōn ἰδού idou τινες tines τῆς tēs κουστωδίας koustōdias ἐλθόντες elthontes εἰς eis τὴν tēn πόλιν polin ἀπήγγειλαν apēngeilan τοῖς tois ἀρχιερεῦσιν archiereusin ἅπαντα hapanta τὰ ta γενόμενα. genomena.
Notes Verse 11

The guard-at-the-tomb apologetic (vv.11-15) — uniquely Matthean. Addresses the Jewish-Christian polemical-context: the body-stolen-by-disciples counter-narrative (preserved in Justin's Dialogue with Trypho 108 and in later rabbinic anti-Christian polemical-tradition). The pericope is generally treated as a 2nd-half-of-1st-c. Matthean-community apologetic-narrative. Davies-Allison ICC 3.666-672.

12
And when they had assembled with the elders and taken counsel together, they gave a sufficient sum of silver to the soldiers,
but the sons of the kingdom shall be cast forth into the outer darkness: there shall be the weeping and the gnashing of teeth.
καὶ kai συναχθέντες synachthentes μετὰ meta τῶν tōn πρεσβυτέρων presbyterōn συμβούλιόν symboulion τε te λαβόντες labontes ἀργύρια argyria ἱκανὰ hikana ἔδωκαν edōkan τοῖς tois στρατιώταις stratiōtais
13
saying, "Tell them, 'His disciples came by night and stole him while we were sleeping.'
And Jesus said unto the centurion, Go thy way; as thou hast believed, [so] be it done unto thee. And the servant was healed in that hour.
λέγοντες· legontes· Εἴπατε Eipate ὅτι hoti Οἱ Hoi μαθηταὶ mathētai αὐτοῦ autou νυκτὸς nyktos ἐλθόντες elthontes ἔκλεψαν eklepsan αὐτὸν auton ἡμῶν hēmōn κοιμωμένων· koimōmenōn·
14
And if this comes to the governor's ears, we will satisfy him and keep you out of trouble."
And when Jesus was come into Peter`s house, he saw his wife`s mother lying sick of a fever.
καὶ kai ἐὰν ean ἀκουσθῇ akousthē τοῦτο touto ἐπὶ epi τοῦ tou ἡγεμόνος, hēgemonos, ἡμεῖς hēmeis πείσομεν peisomen αὐτὸν auton καὶ kai ὑμᾶς hymas ἀμερίμνους amerimnous ποιήσομεν. poiēsomen.
15
So they took the silver and did as they had been taught. And this story has been spread among Jews to this day.
And he touched her hand, and the fever left her; and she arose, and ministered unto him.
οἱ hoi δὲ de λαβόντες labontes τὰ ta ἀργύρια argyria ἐποίησαν epoiēsan ὡς hōs ἐδιδάχθησαν. edidachthēsan. καὶ kai διεφημίσθη diephēmisthē ὁ ho λόγος logos οὗτος houtos παρὰ para Ἰουδαίοις Ioudaiois μέχρι mechri τῆς tēs σήμερον sēmeron ἡμέρας. hēmeras.
16
Now the eleven disciples went into Galilee, to the mountain to which Jesus had directed them.
And when even was come, they brought unto him many possessed with demons: and he cast out the spirits with a word, and healed all that were sick:
Οἱ Hoi δὲ de ἕνδεκα hendeka μαθηταὶ mathētai ἐπορεύθησαν eporeuthēsan εἰς eis τὴν tēn Γαλιλαίαν Galilaian εἰς eis τὸ to ὄρος oros οὗ hou ἐτάξατο etaxato αὐτοῖς autois ὁ ho Ἰησοῦς, Iēsous,
Notes Verse 16

The Great Commission scene opens. Hoi de hendeka mathētai eporeuthēsan eis tēn Galilaian eis to oros hou etaxato autois ho Iēsous — 'the eleven disciples went to Galilee, to the mountain where Jesus had appointed them'. The mountain-as-revelation-site pattern closes the Matthean Gospel (parallel to Mt 5:1 SM-mountain + Mt 17:1 Transfiguration-mountain). See mountain-as-revelation-site-mt-cross-corpus-har-sinai-mount-sapunu. The eleven (hendeka) — Matthias not-yet-elected (cf. Acts 1:15-26).

17
And when they saw him, they worshipped him; but some doubted.
that it might be fulfilled which was spoken through Isaiah the prophet, saying: Himself took our infirmities, and bare our diseases.
καὶ kai ἰδόντες idontes αὐτὸν auton προσεκύνησαν, prosekynēsan, οἱ hoi δὲ de ἐδίστασαν. edistasan.
Notes Verse 17

hoi de edistasan — 'but some doubted'. The Matthean honesty: the resurrection-appearance is met with mixed-response, not unanimous-confession. The historical-honesty parallel to Mk 16:8 (the women's fear-and-flight) + Lk 24:11 (the disciples' disbelief) + Jn 20:25 (Thomas's doubt).

18
And Jesus came up and spoke to them, saying, "All authority has been given to me in heaven and on earth.
Now when Jesus saw great multitudes about him, he gave commandments to depart unto the other side.
καὶ kai προσελθὼν proselthōn ὁ ho Ἰησοῦς Iēsous ἐλάλησεν elalēsen αὐτοῖς autois λέγων· legōn· Ἐδόθη Edothē μοι moi πᾶσα pasa ἐξουσία exousia ἐν en οὐρανῷ ouranō καὶ kai ἐπὶ epi γῆς. gēs.
Notes Verse 18

edothē moi pasa exousia en ouranō kai epi gēs — 'all authority has been given to me in heaven and on earth'. Direct appropriation of Dan 7:13-14 LXX kai edothē autō exousia ... kai pasa tou kosmou ho oikoumenē — the Son-of-Man-enthronement authority-grant. The Risen Jesus' authority-claim explicitly draws on the Dan 7 Son-of-Man tradition. See son-of-man-bar-enash-dan-7-13-mt-cross-corpus and great-commission-mt-28-19-20-trinitarian-baptismal-formula-conybeare-hypothesis-cross-corpus-with-disavowals.

19
Go therefore and make disciples of all the nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,
And there came a scribe, and said unto him, Teacher, I will follow thee whithersoever thou goest.
πορευθέντες poreuthentes οὖν oun μαθητεύσατε mathēteusate πάντα panta τὰ ta ἔθνη, ethnē, βαπτίζοντες baptizontes αὐτοὺς autous εἰς eis τὸ to ὄνομα onoma τοῦ tou πατρὸς patros καὶ kai τοῦ tou υἱοῦ huiou καὶ kai τοῦ tou ἁγίου hagiou πνεύματος, pneumatos,
Notes Verse 19

The Great Commission proper. poreuthentes oun mathēteusate panta ta ethnē, baptizontes autous eis to onoma tou patros kai tou huiou kai tou hagiou pneumatos — 'going therefore, make disciples of all the nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit'. The panta ta ethnē resolves the prior Matthean Israel-only mission-restrictions (Mt 10:5-6; 15:24). The trinitarian baptismal formula is preserved in ALL extant Greek manuscripts including Vaticanus + Sinaiticus + Alexandrinus + the early papyri. The Conybeare 1901 hypothesis that the Eusebian pre-Nicene shorter form en tō onomati mou represents an earlier reading is documented as one scholarly position without adjudication. Three reading-strata preserved (mainstream Christian-tradition / Conybeare-hypothesis / Raëlian-canon Elohim-Son-Spirit reading). Lens-discipline operational disavowals explicitly reject (i) Sitchin / Anunnaki engineered-Elohim-craft pre-resolution, (ii) orientalist / colonialist Great-Commission misreadings, (iii) Raëlian-canon Elohim-Son-Spirit-triad pre-resolution. See great-commission-mt-28-19-20-trinitarian-baptismal-formula-conybeare-hypothesis-cross-corpus-with-disavowals.

20
teaching them to observe all that I have commanded you; and behold, I am with you always, to the consummation of the age.
And Jesus saith unto him, The foxes have holes, and the birds of the heaven [have] nests; but the Son of man hath not where to lay his head.
διδάσκοντες didaskontes αὐτοὺς autous τηρεῖν tērein πάντα panta ὅσα hosa ἐνετειλάμην eneteilamēn ὑμῖν· hymin· καὶ kai ἰδοὺ idou ἐγὼ egō μεθ' meth' ὑμῶν hymōn εἰμι eimi πάσας pasas τὰς tas ἡμέρας hēmeras ἕως heōs τῆς tēs συντελείας synteleias τοῦ tou αἰῶνος. aiōnos.
Notes Verse 20

idou egō meth' hymōn eimi pasas tas hēmeras heōs tēs synteleias tou aiōnos — 'behold, I am with you all the days until the end of the age'. The Matthean Emmanuel-inclusio closes with the abiding-presence promise that echoes Mt 1:23 Meth' hēmōn ho theos ('God with us'). The inclusio is the central Matthean structural-theological framing (Kupp 1996). See emmanuel-frame-inclusio-mt-1-23-mt-28-20-divine-presence-cross-corpus-kupp. The synteleia tou aiōnos (end of the age) eschatological-formula — aiōn as age-pertaining (echoing the Mt 25:41/46 aiōnios usage). The Matthean Gospel closes with the eschatological-presence promise.

Contents

    Wheel of Heaven is an open, multilingual reading of the ancient world's creation traditions — Raëlian, biblical, Mesopotamian, and others — through a single working hypothesis: that the beings called Elohim were a small advanced human civilization that came here, designed life on Earth, and left a record in the religious texts. The reading runs across twelve ages of the precessional cycle, from the project's beginning twenty-two thousand years ago to the present age of disclosure and into the long future the next Great Year is opening. The site is free, source-aware, and built so the work can be checked.
